text:
Alice Nguyen: FYI customer ACME (acct acme-corp) opened an escalation — seeing ~30-60% 502s and intermittent 504s to the hosted inference endpoint since ~10:12 UTC. They noticed spikes when batch jobs hit around 800 rps. Sample curl + response below.

Alice Nguyen: curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hi"}'

Alice Nguyen: response (one of many):
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers",
  "trace_id": "trace-0a1b2c3d"
}
```

Bob Patel (oncall): adding @eng-sre @eng-runtime. Any obvious throttles?

Carl Li (eng-sre): Can you paste the full trace_id(s) and timeframe? Also pinging envoy admin stats: `curl http://envoy-host:9901/stats?filter=cluster\.upstream_zones` etc.

Alice Nguyen: Sent a small bundle of trace ids and request ids to SRE in DM. Attaching a short envoy log snippet we pulled from the host that handled those traces: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] envoy [warning] [upstream] reset reason: connection termination
[2026-03-15T10:12:35Z] envoy [error] upstream reset before response completed, cluster: api-backend, host: 10.2.5.12:443
[2026-03-15T10:12:35Z] auth-proxy [warn] token-verify timed out after 1500ms for request id req-94ab
```

Dana Rivera (eng-runtime): I pulled cluster stats for that window. Seeing `rq_total` high and `cx_overflow`/`rq_pending_overflow` spikes on the api-backend cluster. Also `http2` stream limit hits on several upstream hosts (max_concurrent_streams reached) => Envoy is closing/terminating streams which shows as 502 to the client.

Dana Rivera: envoy admin snapshot (trimmed):
```
cluster.api-backend.upstream_cx_active: 420
cluster.api-backend.upstream_cx_overflow: 73
cluster.api-backend.upstream_rq_pending_overflow: 48
cluster.api-backend.http2.num_streams: 1000
cluster.api-backend.http2.max_concurrent_streams: 256
```

Erin O'Brien (eng-platform): That `max_concurrent_streams: 256` is the culprit on older hosts. We recently pushed an auth token rotation which momentarily increased auth latency; coupling that with bursty client traffic pushed upstream hosts over their `max_concurrent_streams`, causing resets.

Frank Moore (support): Customer reports they only see the errors when they use long streaming requests and when they send bursts from their worker fleet. If they slow to 200 rps the errors largely disappear.

Carl Li: Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase `http2` max_concurrent_streams on the api-backend cluster/hosts, 2) relax Envoy circuit_breakers for that cluster (increase max_connections/max_pending_requests), 3) implement client-side exponential backoff/retry for 502/504, 4) route heavy traffic to a separate pool (dedicated hosts) while we stabilize.

Erin O'Brien: For immediate customer relief I've allowed a temporary override on a subset of hosts to bump `http2_settings.max_concurrent_streams` to 1024 and increased the cluster circuit_breakers to tolerate the spike. Rolling that to 3/5 of the fleet now.

Dana Rivera: Also found auth-proxy logs showing token verification spikes aligned with the first surge. Looks like the billing/auth service had short-lived DB lock contention during credit checks which added ~1s latency. That increased upstream request duration and held open http2 streams longer.

Alice Nguyen: I've updated the customer: told them we're rolling fixes and recommended they enable client retry (idempotent requests only) and to throttle bursts for a 1 hour window. They asked for repro steps so engineering can reproduce.

Frank Moore: Repro steps I used in staging (quick):
```bash
# simulate burst of streaming requests hitting http2 pool
ab -n 8000 -c 200 -p payload.json -T application/json "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
# or use vegeta with many concurrent connections, include Authorization header
```
Note: use long-lived streaming payloads to reproduce stream exhaustion quicker.

Carl Li: Action items and owners: 
- Dana: roll full-fleet config bump for http2/pools (ETA 30m)
- Erin: follow up with infra/billing team to root cause DB contention on token verify (ETA EOD)
- Alice/Frank: notify customer of mitigation and offer to route to dedicated pool if needed (in progress)
- Carl: add circuit_breaker telemetry and alert for `upstream_rq_pending_overflow > 10` (ETA 24h)

Dana Rivera: Patch is pushed to canary with new http2 settings and circuit breaker increases. Monitoring shows error rate down ~80% in canary hosts. Rolling to remainder now.

Erin O'Brien: Billing team confirms a bad index on the credit-check table caused occasional 800-1200ms latencies under burst; they've queued an index fix and will deploy a migration.

Alice Nguyen: Customer updated — errors dropped after our config rollout and they'll do a controlled burst test tomorrow morning. They were appreciative of the fast turnaround :thumbsup:.

Carl Li: We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth. Postmortem to include: (1) why auth rotation exposed DB index issue; (2) why http2 default limits were insufficient for bursts; (3) recommend changes: better token rotate ramping, circuit-breaker autoscaling, and a default client-retry guidance in our docs.

incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-Edge502s (severity: P2). Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INCIDENT-2026-03-15-Edge502s

Alice Nguyen: OK closing this Slack thread; will add postmortem link once writeup is ready.
